## Why mass deletion is unsafe

- Tests execute via GitHub Actions, not web import roots, so they naturally appear unreachable.
- services.plushie_flower_dynamic_planner_v20 is statically unreferenced but is selected dynamically by the active model planner. Deleting it can break validated timing models.
- Older-looking modules may still run through VM systemd units, separate release directories, operator wrappers, timers, private research jobs, feature flags, or fallbacks.
- Dynamic __import__, import_module, exec and eval sites require manual checks.
- Research replay scripts may be needed to reproduce model selection, even when not imported by the public website.

## Retention decisions so far

- Retain current web, bot, poller, audit queue, enabled publisher source, model selectors, health/freshness, V20 dynamic planner, and regression tests.
- Retain final-pair/Chamois and private Japan source pending the actual VM unit/drop-in inventory and specialist cache check.
- Candidate for **separate** historical retirement review: old first-ten installer scripts, V-numbered experiment launchers, and superseded tests **only after** current CI and rollback references are verified.
- Never put live databases, private history, environment values, credentials or evidence ledgers into public Git.

## Retirement gate for every file

1. Verify actual VM service, timer and drop-in source roots, not only example unit files in GitHub.
2. Check static/dynamic imports, scheduled launchers, feature flags, scripts, CI tests and rollback needs.
3. Preserve the exact source in immutable history or private archives before removing it from active code.
4. Test changes in a **separate retirement PR** with full staged web/publisher checks.
5. Use reversible commits; never auto-delete from production.

Status: production reconciliation CI passes; VM metadata report is pending. No deleted legacy code, no main merge, no VM deployment.
